# Structured UX evaluation: heuristic scoring, walkthroughs, dark-pattern scans

Curated by Skill Harbor — @ghaida's Evaluate skill, the diagnostic entry point of the Intent design-strategy system (the UX doctor that diagnoses and refers to specialists): a systematic methodology, not a vague design review. Five core capabilities — heuristic evaluation against Nielsen's 10 heuristics, each scored 0–4 (cosmetic → catastrophic) with specific violations and evidence; cognitive walkthroughs, asking four questions per task step (will the user try the right effect? notice the action is available? associate the action with the effect? see progress afterward? — rated Pass/Hesitation/Failure); anti-pattern detection across the Intent catalog (deceptive patterns, prechecked consent, fake urgency/scarcity, addictive design, attention exploitation, weaponized accessibility, vulnerable-user exploitation, AI-specific dark patterns — dark-pattern findings are always P0 or P1, with regulatory implications noted); task success analysis (completion, efficiency, error rate, recovery, satisfaction — estimated explicitly when no live data exists); and assessment-to-action routing, where every finding maps to the specialist skill that owns the fix (/organize, /articulate, /journey, /fortify, /include, /blueprint, /measure, /investigate, /strategize, /specify, /philosopher). A fixed output format (UX Health Score 0–100, Anti-Pattern Verdict, P0–P3 priority issues, heuristic scores, walkthrough results, positive findings, recommended actions grouped by skill), plus the...
